newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says Italian banks' credit quality mixed.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says Italian banks' credit quality mixed.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday that credit quality in the Italian banking industry remains mixed and it expects divergence in ratings between strong and weak banks to widen.

"The rate of increase in bad loans has slowed, which provides some comfort from a credit perspective," Moody's said in a report on the sector. "But the degree of comfort varies from bank to bank, and from the stronger north of Italy to the weaker south."
Besides stubborn asset-quality problems, Moody's cites weak profitability, the potential for capital erosion, and fading institutional support as causes for concern.
The rating agency also cited some plus signs for the banking system. Moody's said it should benefit in the long term from its regulator-inspired consolidation, although progress is slow.
"Moreover, most rated banks have taken advantage of more favorable conditions in the last two years to stabilize their financial positions," Moody's said.
"Managements are aware of the importance of improving profitability levels, and some have begun to shift emphasis towards profitability, and away from growth for the sake of growth," the report said.

Moody's said growth in bad loans had slowed slightly, to a 16% year-on-year rise at June 1996. "Much of this rise represents ongoing fall-out from poor credit practices during the surge in lending earlier in the decade."
Moody's said preprovision profits are adequate, and comparable with European peers, but it believes net interest margins will come under pressure as domestic competition intensifies.

Regulatory support continues to underpin the overall credit quality of the system, Moody's said. But the public sector's investment in the banking system is being reduced as banking assets are transferred to the private sector.
"As the state disengages from the banking sector, there is a risk that its appetite for intervention may be diminishing," it said.
